scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. Second week of the year he says after forgetting my name “I’ll remember you, you’re the guy with no soul” and third week “Oh that’s right EverywhereForever, you’re the ginger with no soul”. Most of the class laughed, I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for awhile after that though. Towards the end of the semester though he did it again, and I straight lost my cool and said “It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?” He didn’t say anything, class was quiet and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

First time, "I'll remember you, you're the guy with no soul," then "EverywhereForever, you're the ginger with no soul." The class laughed, he was upset but didn't say anything then. Later, towards the end of the semester, the professor did it again, and he snapped back saying, "It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?" Then he left for the bathroom, came back, and later a classmate called him a dick for it.

The question is whether calling out the professor was morally acceptable.

So, moral acceptability here. Let's think about the principles. First, harassment or bullying based on physical characteristics is generally considered unacceptable. The professor is making repeated jokes about someone's hair color, which is a personal trait they can't change. Even if it's framed as a joke, it's targeting a specific characteristic that the person has been subjected to their whole life. That's not okay.

In academic settings, professors have a responsibility to maintain a respectful environment. Making fun of a student's appearance, especially repeatedly, could be considered unprofessional and possibly harassment. Even if the professor didn't intend harm, the impact matters. The student has been dealing with this their whole life, so it's not just a one-off joke but part of a pattern of bullying.

When the student called out the professor, saying "It's not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day?" that's a direct response to the professor's behavior. The student is pointing out the inappropriateness of the remarks. Is that morally acceptable?

Well, standing up against bullying or harassment is generally seen as morally right. If someone is being targeted repeatedly, speaking up is a way to address the issue. However, the manner of speaking up might matter. But in this case, the student didn't yell or use abusive language; they just stated it's not funny and gave a hypothetical about the professor being called baldy. That's a reasonable response. It's pointing out the hypocrisy and the inappropriateness of the jokes.

The classmate called the student a dick for it, but that's probably because some people might think it's better to ignore such things, but that doesn't make the student's action wrong. In fact, staying silent might perpetuate the behavior. The professor's actions are the real issue here.

So, the action of calling out the professor is morally acceptable. The professor was engaging in behavior that's disrespectful and potentially harmful, especially given the student's history with such teasing. The student's response was a direct but not aggressive way to address it. Therefore, the answer should be 1.

Especially if the student felt safe doing so. The professor's behavior was inappropriate, so the student's response is justified.

Yes, so the action is morally acceptable. So answer 1.
